cemd.builders.base.make_solution(box: ~typing.Sequence[float] | numpy.ndarray = [30, 30, 30], density: float = 1.0, solutes_dict: dict[slice(<class 'str'>, <class 'int'>, None)] = None, structures_dict: dict[slice(<class 'str'>, <class 'cemd.core.atomic_system.AtomicSystem'>, None)] = None) → AtomicSystem[source]¶

Generate an AtomicSystem representing a liquid solution using Packmol.

This function automatically determines the number of solvent molecules (H2O) required to reach the target density, accounting for the mass of all provided solutes.

Parameters:

  • box – Dimensions of the simulation box in Angstroms [a, b, c]. Defaults to [30, 30, 30].

  • density – Target density of the solution in g/cm³. Defaults to 1.0.

  • solutes_dict – Dictionary mapping solute names (keys) to their respective counts (values). Keys must match either known monatomic ions or entries in structures_dict.

  • structures_dict – Dictionary mapping solute names to their corresponding AtomicSystem objects for complex molecules or custom structures.

Returns:

The final system geometry generated by Packmol, with configured box parameters and topology.

Return type:

AtomicSystem

Raises:

ValueError – If a solute key is neither a known ion nor found in structures_dict, or if the total mass of solutes exceeds the total mass allowed by the target density and box volume.

Notes

The function currently assumes water (H2O) as the default solvent. Packmol constraints are applied using a 5% safety margin on the box dimensions.

cemd.builders.base.protonate(data: AtomicSystem, atom_index: int, bond_length: float = 1.0) → AtomicSystem[source]¶

Add a proton (hydrogen atom) to a specific atom in the system.

The position of the new proton is calculated to be opposite to the center of mass of the target atom’s current neighbors to respect local geometry (e.g., VSEPR logic).

Parameters:

  • data (AtomicSystem) – The atomic system object to modify.

  • atom_index (int) – The 0-based integer position (iloc) of the target atom in the data.atoms DataFrame.

  • bond_length (float, default 1.0) – The distance between the target atom and the new proton in Ångströms.

  • proton_type (str, default ‘H’) – The type label for the newly created atom.

Returns:

data – The modified atomic system with the added proton and updated types/masses.

Return type:

AtomicSystem

Notes

If the target atom has no neighbors, the proton is placed along the Z-axis. The function automatically updates data.atom_types and data.masses if a new element is introduced.

cemd.builders.hydrates.make_csh(cs_ratio: float, ws_ratio: float, supercell: Sequence[int] = [3, 5, 1], model: str = 'tob11a_hamid.cif', min_mcl=3, progress_callback: Callable[[int, str], None] = None) → AtomicSystem[source]¶

Create a C-S-H supercell. To reach the wanted C/S ratio: first removes bridging SiO2 groups until the minimum meaning chain length (MCL) is reached, then add calcium ions. A fully dimeric silicate structure was not found experimentally and the minimum MCL is close to 3 (see https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520614021982). Subsequently, the packmol code is called to insert water molecules in the interlayer ro reach the given H2O/Si ratio. The relation between C/S and H/S found in experiments (see https://doi.org/10.1107S2052520614021982) is: \(H/S = \frac{19}{17} C/S - \frac{7}{17}\).

Todo

Parameters:

  • cs_ratio – The calcium/silicate ratio of the C-S-H model to be created

  • ws_ratio – The water/silicate ratio of the C-S-H model to be created

  • supercell – A list with the number of replicates of the unit cell in each direction (a, b, c)

  • model – Name of the tobermorite model to use.

    Currently supported: -“tob11a_hamid.cif” -“tob14a_merlino.cif”

  • min_mcl – Minimum mean chain length to keep in the calculation, whatever the C/S ratio.

  • progress_callback – Progress callback for GUI

cemd.builders.hydrates.pycsh(cs_ratio: float, ws_ratio: float, supercell: Sequence = [3, 5, 2], nsamples: int = 1, name=None, seed=None, progress_callback: Callable[[int, str], None] = None) → list[AtomicSystem][source]¶

Create a C-S-H model or a list of C-S-H models as LAMMPSData using the pyCSH code (see https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cemconres.2024.107593).

Parameters:

  • cs_ratio – The calcium/silicate ratio of the C-S-H model to be created

  • ws_ratio – The water/silicate ratio of the C-S-H model to be created

  • supercell – A list with the number of replicates of the unit cell in each direction (a, b, c)

  • nsamples – The number of models to create

  • name – Prefix for the LAMMPSData files

  • seed – Seed for the pyCSH generator

  • progress_callback – Progress callback for GUI
